transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-16
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Starlight CTO), Priya Singh (Infra), Omar Ruiz (Security), Elena Gomez (Partnerships)

Auto-summary: Intro / partner discovery between Redwood and Starlight Cloud. High-level fit: Starlight wants a managed inference partner to offer to their customers and possibly a dedicated Redwood instance on Starlight's GPU farms. Key asks: performance on their Aurora-X GPUs, VPC/private deploy options, SOC2/KMS compatibility, pricing for dedicated capacity. Agreed next steps: SE benchmark, share sizing/pricing, schedule technical deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Liam, our systems engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Raj: Good thanks, Raj here at Starlight Cloud. Appreciate you taking the time.
[00:11] Elena: Hi all, Elena from partnerships, quick intro.
[00:15] Liam: Nice to meet you. Quick agenda: intro, high-level partnership models, technical fit, security questions, and next steps. Sound good?
[00:22] Priya: Yup, that works. We have about 40 minutes so appreciate keeping to that.
[00:30] Maya: Great. To kick off can you give us a bit of background on Starlight's product and why you're looking at inference partners?
[00:38] Raj: Sure. We're an edge-first cloud targeting media and real-time apps. Recently customers asked for low-latency LLM inference at the edge, and we're evaluating partners to offer a managed inference product vs building in-house. Key for us is latency, cost, and the ability to offer a dedicated option to enterprise customers.
[00:58] Maya: Makes sense. Do you have existing customers running models today or is this pre-prod?
[01:03] Raj: A few pilot customers running smaller models on-host, but nothing production. We're targeting pilots in Q3 and GA in Q4.
[01:10] Liam: When you say low-latency, what's the expected SLO and QPS? Ballpark is fine.
[01:16] Priya: For real-time media features we need P95 latency <= 120ms for short prompts, and some customers want sustained 50-100 qps per region. Depends on model size obviously.
[01:28] Liam: Got it, that's helpful. We typically route by latency policy, and for those constraints we'd look at smaller optimized model variants or lower batch sizes to hit P95.
[01:38] Maya: Also curious about your infra — I know you run Aurora-X GPUs in multiple regions? Any constraints around networking or VPCs?
[01:47] Raj: Yes, we're on Aurora-X hardware in our edge zones. Networking-wise we prefer VPC peering or private link for enterprise customers. Multi-tenant hosted is ok for some enterprises but larger ones demand dedicated capacity and data isolation.
[02:01] Omar: From security side we need SOC2 compliance, SSO via SAML, and KMS integration. Also audit logs for inference requests; retention TBD.
[02:12] Liam: That's all within Redwood's common asks. We support SAML/SSO, KMS integrations and audit logs. For private deployments we can do a private control plane with customer-managed networking. There may be some naming differences in the transcript; I might say "private control plane" or "private deploy" interchangeably.
[02:28] Raj: Great. On the model side, do you host open models only or can you bring customer-provided models?
[02:34] Maya: We support curated open models and customers can bring their own weights, subject to licensing. For dedicated and private deployments you can pin versions. We also have Redwood Optimize to recommend quantization and batching to hit cost targets.
[02:48] Priya: What about on-prem or air-gapped? Some regulated customers may require that.
[02:53] Liam: We have an on-prem package and can run the private control plane in your VPC or in an air-gapped environment with the right networking and support contract.
[03:02] Raj: Ok, good. Pricing question: do you do reserved capacity? We expect some customers will want predictable monthly commits.
[03:09] Maya: Yes, Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. There's usage-based for hosted API as well. I'll send a draft pricing sheet after this call.
[03:17] Elena: On partnership models, we're thinking about two tracks: 1) integration where Starlight offers Redwood as a managed add-on to customers (co-sell/marketplace), and 2) deeper resell where we might bundle in our infrastructure. Curious what you've done with other partners.
[03:31] Liam: We've done both. For marketplace listings we help with integration and performance profiles; for resell we coordinate billing and support SLAs. There are tradeoffs re: billing complexity and quoting.
[03:41] Maya: For technical validation, we'd like to run a benchmark on your Aurora-X hardware with a couple of representative workloads to measure latency and cost-per-inference. Would that be possible?
[03:51] Priya: Yes, we can provision a test cluster and provide access. We'll need to coordinate security and data access; Omar will want to sign off.
[03:58] Omar: Correct. We'll likely want a dedicated test VPC and temporary credentials, plus an NDA or lab access agreement.
[04:06] Liam: Totally reasonable. We can run the benchmark in a few configurations: hosted on your machines with Redwood Dedicated runtime, and private on a VPC with our control plane. We'll capture token-level latency and cost breakdown.
[04:20] Raj: What about model compatibility and kernel optimizations for Aurora-X?
[04:25] Liam: The runtime selects optimized kernels based on model architecture and seq lengths. For new hardware we do kernel selection and sometimes small tuning passes. We'll want some time to validate but it's a standard onboarding flow.
[04:36] Maya: Quick note: sometimes our docs or speech say KV "cash" instead of cache in transcripts; just ignore that if it appears.
[04:43] (laughs)
[04:47] Raj: Ha, noted.
[04:50] Maya: On data residency, any region requirements?
[04:53] Raj: Europe customers need data residency in eu-central and a few APAC customers want regional coverage.
[04:59] Liam: We can pin routing by region and provide regional dedicated pools. For GA we'll need to plan capacity in those zones.
[05:07] Priya: Another thing: some customers will push for lower precision / quantized models to reduce costs. How do you handle quantization?
[05:15] Liam: We have quantization-friendly execution paths and can recommend profiles per workload. Redwood Optimize will give suggestions and expected perf gains. For some models we run int8 or custom quant profiles.
[05:26] Raj: Good. Any blockers around licensing if customers want to run closed-source weights?
[05:31] Maya: We require proof of licensing for commercial weights and will follow customer bring-your-own model policies. For private deployments it's generally straightforward but we validate T&Cs.
[05:40] Elena: From GTM, if we co-sell, what materials do you provide? Playbooks? Benchmarks?
[05:46] Maya: Yes, partner playbooks, reference architectures, and verified performance profiles. We'll also put a partner listing in the marketplace if we agree.
[05:55] Raj: Timeline-wise we said pilots in Q3. What's a realistic kickoff timeline for a benchmark?
[06:01] Liam: If you can provide test access and sample prompts within a week, we can run a first-pass benchmark within 7-10 business days. Then deeper tuning may take another 2-3 weeks.
[06:12] Priya: Sounds fine. Omar, anything else from security?
[06:15] Omar: Yes; KMS integration for key wrapping, HSM if needed, retention policy for audit logs. Also penetration test requirements for private deployments.
[06:23] Liam: We support KMS integrations and HSM is an add-on. Pen tests are typically arranged through our security team; we can share scope and previous reports.
[06:31] Maya: I'll attach SOC2 summary and a KMS integration doc. Liam will follow up with a benchmark plan and required credentials.
[06:38] Raj: Great. A few technical clarifications: do you support streaming outputs and function/tool-calls? Some of our customers need streaming for real-time chat features.
[06:47] Liam: Yes, the platform supports streaming responses and tool-calling primitives. We'll test streaming latency as part of the benchmark.
[06:53] Priya: For the benchmark, which models do you recommend we test first?
[06:57] Liam: For low-latency workloads maybe a 7B optimized variant and a 13B quantized variant so we can see tradeoffs. If you have a specific customer model, bring that too.
[07:08] Raj: We'll start with the 7B/13B.
[07:11] (short pause)
[07:20] Maya: Are there any commercial constraints: reseller agreement, revenue share, or marketplace fees you expect?
[07:26] Elena: We haven't locked that down yet. We'd like to see typical partner terms from Redwood to compare.
[07:32] Maya: We can share a partner agreement template and typical revenue share tiers.
[07:36] Raj: Ok thanks.
[07:40] (timestamp jump — mid-meeting details, roughly 20 minutes in)
[20:05] Liam: Quick technical aside on KV caching, we can do prefix caching to reduce token costs for repeated prompts. That will affect hit rates; we'll need representative prompt datasets to simulate.
[20:18] Priya: We'll provide a sample set of repeated prompts for caching tests.
[20:23] Raj: Also curious about autoscaling. If a customer has bursty traffic, can Dedicated handle bursts?
[20:30] Maya: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity options. For strict SLOs we can provision extra headroom or automatic fallbacks to a compatible hosted model variant.
[20:42] Liam: Right, and smart routing can fallback by model size or region if capacity is constrained. There's always a cost/latency tradeoff.
[20:50] Omar: For audit logs, how granular are they? Token-level? Request-level? We need to plan storage.
[20:56] Liam: We provide per-request metadata and can capture token-level cost breakdowns. Retention windows are configurable; long-term export to your SIEM is supported.
[21:07] Priya: About networking: VPC peering vs PrivateLink — which do you prefer?
[21:12] Liam: VPC peering gives the lowest latency but requires network config. PrivateLink can be simpler but may add small latency. We'll work with your infra team.
[21:21] Raj: We're okay doing peering for enterprise customers.
[21:25] Elena: One more question on branding: if we're listing in the marketplace, do you allow joint marketing?
[21:31] Maya: Yes, joint webinars, case studies, and co-branded collateral are common.
[21:35] (late meeting — wrap-up)
[35:10] Maya: Ok to recap: 1) Redwood to send sizing guide, pricing and partner terms; 2) Redwood SE to run benchmark on Aurora-X once Starlight provides test access; 3) Starlight to share sample prompts and security requirements; 4) schedule SE deep dive next week — does that capture it?
[35:28] Raj: Yep that covers it.
[35:31] Priya: We'll aim to get the sample data and access details by Monday.
[35:36] Omar: We'll review SOC2/KMS requirements and get back with any blockers.
[35:40] Liam: I'll put together a benchmark plan and a short checklist of what we need for the test cluster.
[35:46] Elena: And I'll coordinate GTM items with Maya.
[35:50] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with docs and calendar invites.
[35:56] Raj: Thanks, talk soon.
[41:38] Meeting end

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and shorthand (e.g., "KV cash" instead of cache).
